findings.summary: Excluding equity gains makes non-GAAP earnings more useful for comparing operating performance, but less complete as a measure of total earnings.
findings.text: The equity-gain adjustments were {{fact:NVDA:cash_bridge:equity_security_gains_adjustment:current}} currently and {{fact:NVDA:cash_bridge:equity_security_gains_adjustment:prior_quarter}} earlier. Larger earlier gains boosted the GAAP earnings baseline; excluding them makes the underlying earnings comparison less sensitive to investment gains. NVIDIA also excludes other items and applies associated tax adjustments, so the entire GAAP versus non-GAAP difference cannot be attributed to equity gains alone.

evidence.quote: These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable.

findings.summary: Non-GAAP earnings now include stock-based compensation, and presented historical comparisons have been updated to match.
findings.text: Retaining stock-based compensation recognizes an employee compensation expense rather than removing it merely because it is noncash. Updating the presented historical figures improves consistency across periods. Comparisons against older, unrevised non-GAAP figures would mix accounting treatments. The revised measure remains adjusted earnings, not a substitute for GAAP earnings or operating cash flow.

evidence.quote: Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA’s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense.

takeaway.text: The supplied non-GAAP comparison is useful for assessing earnings without equity-gain volatility while retaining stock-based compensation costs. Use the updated historical series and read it alongside GAAP results; it does not capture all economic gains or measure cash generation.

next_investigation.question: Why is stock-based compensation retained in non-GAAP earnings but added back in operating cash flow?
next_investigation.new_information: The answer establishes that adjusted earnings retain compensation expense. This follow-up explains the distinct cash-flow reconciliation purpose of adding back a noncash expense, clarifying why the treatments are not contradictory.
